newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK producer prices show inflation subdued.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK producer prices show inflation subdued.

text.p: Prices of British factory gate goods were flat in August while raw material costs edged up only modestly, painting a rosy picture of inflation in the months ahead, official figures showed on Monday.

The Producer Price Index showed unadjusted output prices were flat during the month, with a two percent rise on the same month last year. This was bang in line with financial market forecasts and was the lowest yearly increase since July 1994.
At the same time, costs of raw materials used in British manufacturing edged up by 0.3 percent, allowing the input price component to fall by a yearly rate of 2.2 percent.
It was the third consecutive fall this year and came despite a sharp surge in the oil price component of the index, which was up by 3.5 percent on the month and 28.4 percent on the year.

"These are excellent figures, particularly impressive when you bear in mind several adverse factors, notably the rise in global oil prices," Sakura Finance economist Mark Hale said. Britain's Treasury welcomed the data.

"The fall in output and input inflation to very low levels gives British manufacturers even better opportunities to sell goods abroad and brings good news for the inflation outlook at home," Treasury Economic Secretary Angela Knight said. August figures for the retail price index, Britain's main inflation indicator, are due on Thursday. Most are forecasting small falls in the yearly measure of both headline and underlying inflation, which excludes volatile home loan costs.

Some economists believe the PPI index boosts the government's chances of meeting its tough 2.5 percent underlying inflation target by the time its current term in office ends early in 1997. A general election is due by May 1997.
Views were mixed on whether the data increase the scope for another cut in the 5-3/4 percent official base interest rate.
"These are good numbers but not enough on their own to prompt a rate cut just yet," HSBC economist Ian Sheperdson said.

Other analysts believe it will strengthen Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's hand in pushing for the fifth rate cut in a year at his September 23 monetary meeting with Bank of England governor Eddie George.
"Coming just a few days before the next party conference season gets underway, such a move would inevitably carry political overtones," CIBC economist David Coleman noted.
The embattled ruling Conservatives, who are far behind the Opposition Labour party in opinion polls, are struggling to reap the benefits of economic recovery.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the sharp rise in oil prices during August was more than offset by falls in the prices of rubber, paper and seasonal food.
But analysts noted that a delay in allowing Iraq to sell oil for food in retaliation for Iraqi attacks on Kurdish rebels would increase the pressure on global crude prices.
Core output prices excluding the volatile food, drink tobacco and petrol component were also flat in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, the ONS said.
Unadjusted output prices were also flat on the month while the 1.2 percent yearly rise was the lowest since October 1967.
